Convergence in 𝑚

Last modified: 05-10-2025.

To observe convergence in \(m\), we calibrate \(h\) and \(\tau\) to \(m\) as \(h \sim e^{-\pi\sqrt{(1-\alpha/2)m}}\) and then \(\tau \sim h^{\alpha}\), respectively. With this scaling, the convergence with respect to the rational order \(m\) is exponential. That is, \(\|u-U_{h,m}^\tau\|_{L_2((0,T);L_2(\Gamma))} \leq C_me^{-\alpha\pi\sqrt{(1-\alpha/2)m}}\). This can be verified by estimating the slope \(S_m\) in the regression \(\log_e E = S_m\sqrt{m} +\log_e C_m\), where we expect \(S_m\sim -\alpha\pi\sqrt{(1-\alpha/2)}\).

# remotes::install_github("davidbolin/rspde", ref = "devel")
# remotes::install_github("davidbolin/metricgraph", ref = "devel")
library(rSPDE)
library(MetricGraph)
library(grateful)

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(plotly)
library(slackr)
source("keys.R")
slackr_setup(token = token) # token comes from keys.R
## [1] "Successfully connected to Slack"
capture.output(
  knitr::purl(here::here("functionality.Rmd"), output = here::here("functionality.R")),
  file = here::here("purl_log.txt")
)
source(here::here("functionality.R"))
# Parameters
T_final <- 2
kappa <- 4
divider <- 7
N_finite = 4 # choose even
adjusted_N_finite <- N_finite + N_finite/2 + 1
# Coefficients for u_0 and f
coeff_U_0 <- 50*(1:adjusted_N_finite)^-1
coeff_U_0[-5] <- 0
coeff_FF <- rep(0, adjusted_N_finite)
coeff_FF[7] <- 10

AAA = 1
OMEGA = pi

# Time step and mesh size
m_vector <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
alpha_vector <- seq(1, 1.8, by = 0.2)
# Enforce nestedness
hs <- c()
for (j in 1:length(alpha_vector)) {
  alpha <- alpha_vector[j]
  for (i in 1:length(m_vector)) {
    m <- m_vector[i]
    h <- exp(- pi * sqrt((1 - alpha / 2) * m))/divider 
    time_step <- (h^alpha)
    hs <- c(hs, h)
  }}
min_hs <- min(hs)
min_hs
## [1] 0.001680283
# Truncate to first significant digit
min_hs_trunc <- trunc_first_signi_digit(min_hs)
min_hs_trunc
## [1] 0.001
graphs <- list()
aux_graph <- gets.graph.tadpole(h = min_hs_trunc)
graphs[[1]] <- aux_graph$mesh$V
counter <- 1
for (j in 1:length(alpha_vector)) {
  alpha <- alpha_vector[j]
  for (i in 1:length(m_vector)) {
    m <- m_vector[i]
    h <- exp(- pi * sqrt((1 - alpha / 2) * m))/divider 
    time_step <- (h^alpha)
    h_aux <- largest_nested_h(min_hs_trunc, h)
    print(paste0("m = ", m, ", h_cand = ", formatC(h, format = "f", digits = 6), ", h_aux = ", h_aux, ", h_aux/h_fine = ", h_aux/min_hs_trunc, ", tau = ", formatC(time_step, format = "f", digits = 6)))
    counter <- counter + 1
    aux_graph <- gets.graph.tadpole(h = h_aux)
    graphs[[counter]] <- aux_graph$mesh$V
  }}
## [1] "m = 1, h_cand = 0.015493, h_aux = 0.01, h_aux/h_fine = 10, tau = 0.015493"
## [1] "m = 2, h_cand = 0.006173, h_aux = 0.005, h_aux/h_fine = 5, tau = 0.006173"
## [1] "m = 3, h_cand = 0.003047, h_aux = 0.002, h_aux/h_fine = 2, tau = 0.003047"
## [1] "m = 4, h_cand = 0.001680, h_aux = 0.001, h_aux/h_fine = 1, tau = 0.001680"
## [1] "m = 1, h_cand = 0.019588, h_aux = 0.01, h_aux/h_fine = 10, tau = 0.008921"

## [1] "m = 2, h_cand = 0.019588, h_aux = 0.01, h_aux/h_fine = 10, tau = 0.001850"
## [1] "m = 3, h_cand = 0.012533, h_aux = 0.01, h_aux/h_fine = 10, tau = 0.000906"
## [1] "m = 4, h_cand = 0.008601, h_aux = 0.008, h_aux/h_fine = 8, tau = 0.000496"
## [1] "m = 1, h_cand = 0.052899, h_aux = 0.05, h_aux/h_fine = 50, tau = 0.005037"
## [1] "m = 2, h_cand = 0.035054, h_aux = 0.025, h_aux/h_fine = 25, tau = 0.002402"
## [1] "m = 3, h_cand = 0.025562, h_aux = 0.025, h_aux/h_fine = 25, tau = 0.001360"
## [1] "m = 4, h_cand = 0.019588, h_aux = 0.01, h_aux/h_fine = 10, tau = 0.000843"
# Combine matrices into one data frame with a "group" column
df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(graphs), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    x = graphs[[i]][,1],
    y = graphs[[i]][,2],
    group = as.factor(i)   # group indicates which list member
  )
}))

# Plot
p_graphs <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Points colored by list member", color = "List Member")
plotly::ggplotly(p_graphs)
# Overkill parameters
overkill_time_step <- 0.1 * 2^-14
overkill_h <- min_hs_trunc #(0.1 * 2^-14)^(1/2)
# Finest time and space mesh
overkill_time_seq <- seq(0, T_final, length.out = ((T_final - 0) / overkill_time_step + 1))
overkill_graph <- gets.graph.tadpole(h = overkill_h)
# Compute the weights on the finest mesh
overkill_graph$compute_fem() # This is needed to compute the weights
overkill_weights <- overkill_graph$mesh$weights
overkill_C <- overkill_graph$mesh$C
# Create a matrix to store the errors
errors_projected <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(m_vector), ncol = length(alpha_vector))
for (j in 1:length(alpha_vector)) {
  alpha <- alpha_vector[j] # from 0.5 to 2
  beta <- alpha / 2

  # Compute the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions on the finest mesh
  overkill_eigen_params <- gets.eigen.params(N_finite = N_finite, kappa = kappa, alpha = alpha, graph = overkill_graph)
  EIGENVAL_ALPHA <- overkill_eigen_params$EIGENVAL_ALPHA # Eigenvalues (they are independent of the meshes)
  overkill_EIGENFUN <- overkill_eigen_params$EIGENFUN # Eigenfunctions on the finest mesh
  
  # Compute the true solution on the finest mesh
  overkill_U_true <- overkill_EIGENFUN %*% 
    outer(1:length(coeff_U_0), 
          1:length(overkill_time_seq), 
          function(i, j) (coeff_U_0[i] + coeff_FF[i] * G_sin(t = overkill_time_seq[j], A = AAA, lambda_j_alpha_half = EIGENVAL_ALPHA[i], omega = OMEGA)) * exp(-EIGENVAL_ALPHA[i] * overkill_time_seq[j]))
  
  for (i in 1:length(m_vector)) {
    m <- m_vector[i]
    h <- exp(- pi * sqrt((1 - alpha / 2) * m))/divider 
    time_step <- (h^alpha)
    h <- largest_nested_h(min_hs_trunc, h)
    
    graph <- gets.graph.tadpole(h = h)
    graph$compute_fem()
    G <- graph$mesh$G
    C <- graph$mesh$C
    L <- kappa^2*C + G
    eigen_params <- gets.eigen.params(N_finite = N_finite, kappa = kappa, alpha = alpha, graph = graph)
    EIGENFUN <- eigen_params$EIGENFUN
    U_0 <- EIGENFUN %*% coeff_U_0 # Compute U_0 on the current mesh
    Psi <- graph$fem_basis(overkill_graph$get_mesh_locations())
  
    time_seq <- seq(0, T_final, length.out = ((T_final - 0) / time_step + 1))
    my_op_frac <- my.fractional.operators.frac(L, beta, C, scale.factor = kappa^2, m = m, time_step)
    INT_BASIS_EIGEN <- t(overkill_EIGENFUN) %*% overkill_graph$mesh$C %*% Psi
    # Compute matrix F with columns F^k
    FF_approx <- t(INT_BASIS_EIGEN) %*% 
      outer(1:length(coeff_FF), 
            1:length(time_seq), 
        function(i, j) coeff_FF[i] * g_sin(r = time_seq[j], A = AAA, omega = OMEGA))

    U_approx <- solve_fractional_evolution(my_op_frac, time_step, time_seq, val_at_0 = U_0, RHST = FF_approx)
    projected_U_approx <- Psi %*% U_approx
    projected_U_piecewise <- construct_piecewise_projection(projected_U_approx, time_seq, overkill_time_seq)
    XX <- overkill_U_true - projected_U_piecewise
    errors_projected[i,j] <- sqrt(as.double(overkill_time_step * sum(XX * (overkill_graph$mesh$C %*% XX)))) 
    slackr_msg(text = paste0("m =", m, ", alpha =", alpha, ", h =", h, ", time_step =", time_step), channel = "#research")
  }
}
save(errors_projected, file = here::here("data_files/errors_projected_m.RData"))
load(here::here("data_files/errors_projected_m.RData"))
observed_rates <- numeric(length(alpha_vector))
for (u in 1:length(alpha_vector)) {
  observed_rates[u] <- coef(lm(log(errors_projected[, u]) ~ sqrt(m_vector)))[2]
}

theoretical_rates <- - pi * alpha_vector * sqrt((1 - alpha_vector / 2))

p_m <- error.convergence.plotter(x_axis_vector = m_vector, 
                                 alpha_vector, 
                                 errors_projected, 
                                 theoretical_rates, 
                                 observed_rates,
                                 line_equation_fun = exp_line_equation,
                                 fig_title = expression("Convergence in " * italic(m)),
                                 x_axis_label = expression(italic(m)),
                                 apply_sqrt = TRUE)
p_m

Figure 1: Comparison of theoretical and observed convergence behavior for the \(L_2((0,T);L_2(\Gamma))\)-error with respect to \(m\) on a semi-\(\text{log}_{e}\) scale, with \(m\) plotted on a square-root scale. Dashed lines indicate the theoretical rates, and solid lines represent the observed error curves. The legend below each plot shows the value of \(\alpha\) along with the corresponding theoretical (‘theo’), and observed (‘obs’) rates for each case. 

ggsave(here::here("data_files/conv_rates_m.png"), width = 4, height = 5, plot = p_m, dpi = 300)
save(p_m, file = here::here("data_files/p_m.RData"))
